text.arabic_uthmani: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِى غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكْرِى وَكَانُوا۟ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا

baseline.text: Onların gözleri beni anmaya karşı bir örtü içindeydi ve işitmeye güç yetiremiyorlardı.

findings.text: Anmadan tekrar tekrar yüz çevirmek, görme ve işitme duyularını anlamaya karşı örten kalıcı bir yetersizliğe dönüşür; bu kapanma mağaradaki geçici koruyucu uykunun tersidir.

activation_trace.role: The seeing organ supplies the visual channel that is placed inside the obstruction.
A covering literally screens what lies beneath and functions as the visual barrier.
A reminder makes something present again and identifies the blocked content rather than an absent stimulus.
Capacity and effective ability locate the failure in making receptive hearing occur.
Hearing as understanding, acceptance, and compliance supplies the response that cannot be completed.

changed_reading.after: Their perceptual system cannot convert an available reminder into recognition and compliant understanding.
changed_reading.before: They suffer a generic combination of blindness and deafness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joins eyes enclosed from the reminder to an inability to perform samʿ.
baseline_models.mechanism: A visual barrier is specified relationally as being from the reminder, while hearing names understanding and compliance as well as sound perception. Capacity is therefore blocked at the point where reminder would become receptive response, not merely at two unrelated sense organs.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence and presence in time frame both sensory clauses as one established condition.
Something rising or abounding until it covers what is below turns the barrier into an enveloping medium.
Direct eyewitnessing supplies the mode of access that enclosure prevents.
Auditory perception supplies the second access channel held inside the same state description.

changed_reading.after: They inhabit an enclosing perceptual condition in which neither witnessing nor receptive hearing gains purchase.
changed_reading.before: A momentary distraction keeps them from attending.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired kānat and kānū clauses hold both the covered eyes and failed hearing in one stated condition.
baseline_models.mechanism: The eyes are not said merely to meet a passing obstacle; they are in a covering whose branch image can overwhelm what lies beneath. The repeated state construction makes enclosure and failed auditory uptake a configuration of being.

activation_trace.role: Sending air into something supplies the blast that makes an acoustic event operative in the scene.
The horn of blowing specifies the instrument and makes the contrast with denied hearing concrete.
Joining the dispersed into a gathered whole shows that the preceding event has an effective outcome.
Understanding and compliance identify the kind of hearing still absent despite the operative blast.

changed_reading.after: Sound can operate around and upon them, yet it cannot become understanding, acceptance, or obedience.
changed_reading.before: They are physiologically unable to register sound.

context_deltas.mechanism: An operative blast precedes the focus and is followed by successful gathering. This makes the focus denial sharper if samʿ is the responsive understanding or obedience that sound should elicit, rather than bare arrival of sound at an ear.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a blown horn, gathering, and samʿ as understanding or compliance; I infer that the negation targets receptive uptake. A live alternative is that divine gathering requires no auditory registration at all.
structural_cues: 18:99 places the blown horn and gathering two ayat before the focus, so the local scene already contains effective sound.

activation_trace.role: Bringing something out for viewing supplies public exposure rather than hidden evidence.
Covering or concealing supplies an enacted counterpart to the cover located over the audience's eyes.
Eyewitnessing is the access mode that should answer a display but remains unavailable.
The screening cover relocates concealment from the displayed object to the perceiving eye.

changed_reading.after: The warning may be laid fully before them; the concealment is reproduced in the perceiver's stance and sensory enclosure.
changed_reading.before: They fail because the warning was not visible or sufficiently presented.

context_deltas.mechanism: The warning object is emphatically displayed, while the named audience carries a covering branch and the focus locates covering at their eyes. Evidence can therefore be fully exposed while recognition remains blocked at the receiver.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies emphatic display, a covering branch for kufr, and covered eyes; I infer a receiver-side failure of recognition. Alternatively, the display may be purely judicial and need not describe an earlier epistemic opportunity.
structural_cues: 18:100 immediately precedes the relative clause in 18:101 and repeats ʿaraḍa as verb and cognate object.

activation_trace.role: Taking as an acquisition supplies the deliberate adoption of a relational arrangement.
Otherness or substitution marks the route as displaced from its proper addressee.
Taking charge and governing supplies the alternative authority through which response is routed.
Compliance and following make the denied capacity an allegiance-bearing act, not only a sensory reflex.
Hearing as acceptance and obedience provides the response diverted by substituted guardianship.

changed_reading.after: Their capacity for allegiance is occupied elsewhere, making them unable to render the reminder into its proper obedience.
changed_reading.before: They lack a general ability to obey.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following ayah depicts acquired guardianship directed to others besides God. Because focus hearing includes acceptance and obedience, its incapacity can be read as selective routing: allegiance remains active, but not toward the reminder.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adopted alternative guardians and hearing as obedience; I infer that allegiance channels receptivity away from the reminder. A live alternative is that false guardianship and failed hearing are parallel charges without a directional link.
structural_cues: 18:102 follows the focus with a false calculation that servants can be taken as awliyāʾ besides God.

activation_trace.role: Departure from the intended way supplies the misdirection of otherwise active effort.
Supposition or calculation supplies the internal judgment that seals the activity against correction.
Making something as a product supplies visible output that can be mistaken for successful reception.
Bodily swelling from unwholesome grazing supplies a material image of enlarged but corrupted output.
Measured weight tests whether the apparently enlarged work has real substance.
The reminder is the corrective input excluded from the productive loop.
Understanding and acceptance are the missing feedback operation that could redirect the work.

changed_reading.after: Failed receptive hearing can power a self-confirming production system whose swollen output is exposed as weightless.
changed_reading.before: Failed hearing leaves them inert and unproductive.

context_deltas.mechanism: The covered receiver is not inactive: effort strays while its owners calculate that they manufacture well. The work then carries the branch image of swelling from bad intake and finally receives no weight, forming a loop in which blocked correction permits deceptive productivity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies misdirected effort, self-approval, manufacture, distension, and weighing; I infer a feedback loop in which failure to receive correction lets bad intake become impressive output. Alternatively, these may be sequential verdicts rather than a causal process.
structural_cues: 18:103-105 moves continuously from greatest loss, to confident manufacture, to collapsed works and denied weight.

activation_trace.role: The vast quantity of sea water supplies the largest local image of communicative material.
Ink that continually supplies a pen turns material extension into a model of sustained transmission.
Intelligible speech connecting speakers identifies the content whose supply outlasts its medium.
Exhaustion and ending test the medium while leaving the words beyond exhaustion.
Effective capacity locates the limiting factor at the receiving side.
Auditory uptake is the narrow endpoint contrasted with the unbounded communicative source.

changed_reading.after: The source can exceed oceanic media; the finite obstruction is the receiver's capacity to let speech become hearing.
changed_reading.before: Their failure might reflect insufficient warning or communicative supply.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sea-and-ink sequence makes communicative supply effectively inexhaustible: the medium and its replenishment fail before the words do. Against that abundance, the focus incapacity is a receiver bottleneck, not a shortage of reminder or speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exhaustible medium, replenishment, inexhaustible words, and focus-side incapacity; I infer that the scarcity lies in reception. A live alternative is that 18:109 magnifies the words without commenting on the mechanics of 18:101.
structural_cues: 18:109 repeats sea, words, and exhaustion before adding another supply, near the close of the same context window.

activation_trace.role: The exposed skin or surface supplies the messenger's immediately visible human aspect.
Knowledge cast secretly supplies the nonvisible disclosure that must be received through the visible bearer.
The viewing organ anchors the risk of stopping at what is outwardly visible.
An epistemic cover supplies the failure to pass from surface perception to disclosed meaning.
Understanding and acceptance are the inward uptake that surface fixation fails to achieve.

changed_reading.after: The cover may trap perception at the messenger's visible human surface so that concealed disclosure never becomes understood hearing.
changed_reading.before: The cover simply hides an external religious object.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing ayah places an ordinary visible human surface beside knowledge cast in concealment. The focus coupling of covered eyes and failed understanding can therefore describe fixation at the visible bearer that never receives the hidden disclosure carried through him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies visible humanity, hidden disclosure, and the focus's visual-auditory lock; I infer a surface-to-meaning threshold. Alternatively, the ayah does not state that the audience's failure arose from fixation on the messenger's humanity.
structural_cues: 18:110 directly juxtaposes 'a human like you' with 'revealed to me' before requiring action.

remaining_uncertainties: The horn may gather without requiring any auditory uptake, so it sharpens but does not prove the semantic shift in samʿ.
Alternative allegiance and self-approving work may be consequences or parallel descriptions rather than causes of failed hearing.
The split-root propagation and garden-cover contrast should remain explicitly exploratory in downstream prose.
strongest_changes: The preceding horn and gathering make samʿ primarily failed responsive uptake rather than simple acoustic deafness.
Emphatic display beside kufr's covering branch relocates concealment from missing evidence to the receiver.
Confident manufacture, bad-intake distension, and denied weight turn the sensory failure into a self-sealing production loop.
The inexhaustible words sequence makes communicative scarcity receiver-side rather than source-side.
summary.what_was_special: The focus became a model of obstructed conversion: visible display and abundant speech remain operative, but reminder cannot cross into recognition, correction, and obedient response. The packet also preserved a form-distant propagation image and a contained contrast between harmful and sheltering covers.

activation_trace.role: Extension or rising through the air supplies a form-distant image of hearing failing to propagate.
An abundance rising over what lies beneath supplies the medium through which propagation fails.
Causing another to hear supplies the outward or transmissive edge of the failed act.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, no hearing signal rises, extends, or crosses the enclosing medium into a transmissible response.
changed_reading.before: The clause only negates an inward faculty.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the packet's mapped s-ṭ-ʿ branch is form-distant from the dominant ṭ-w-ʿ analysis. It remains anchored to yastaṭīʿūna, the exact split target supplied by the packet, and the adjacent samʿ; downstream prose should call it an exploratory propagation image, not a lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The sequence lā yastaṭīʿūna samʿan joins the split mapped target's rising extension to an act of hearing under an overwhelming cover.

activation_trace.role: A screening cover supplies the harmful enclosure because its relation is away from remembrance.
A garden covered by vegetation supplies a contrasting enclosure that shelters cultivated life.
Provision prepared for a guest turns the cultivated cover into receptive lodging rather than blockage.

changed_reading.after: The decisive feature is the cover's function and relation: one seals perception away from reminder, while another shelters fruitful reception.
changed_reading.before: Any form of covering is intrinsically deprivation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The analogy is cross-root and surprising: ghitāʾ and jannah are not synonyms. It remains valid as a material contrast because both cited branches explicitly cover, while one blocks remembrance and the other forms cultivated lodging; downstream prose should present a contrast of functions, never an etymological equivalence.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus specifies not covering in the abstract but a covering positioned away from the reminder.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Incapacity to hear is the endpoint of covered attention.** `ذ ك ر` B009 (“reminder or admonition”) is screened from sight, and `ط و ع` B001’s yielding capacity is denied for hearing. This completes the feedback begun in 18:57, where turning away precedes assigned covers and ear-weight. I infer that repeated non-reception becomes embodied inability. Unlike the cave sleepers’ temporary closure, this blockage has no protected awakening function.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:102 connected covered reminder and failed hearing to the false reckoning that servants could protect independently.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Ignorance maintained as a sensory cover.** `غ ط و/B001` is a covering screen; `غ ط و/B005` is a cover of ignorance. The prior ayah forces hell into view, while 18:102 exposes their false ally calculation and 18:104 says they suppose their making is good. I infer that covered sight and disabled hearing are not isolated deficits but the perceptual mechanism that lets mistaken evaluation persist. `فِي غِطَاءٍ عَن ذِكْرِي` reads as an inhabited filtering condition, not momentary inattention.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:102 exposed the false ally calculation and 18:104 the false craft calculation, showing one perceptual cover sustaining errors across worship and work.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative pronoun linking 18:101 to its prior antecedent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) opens 18:101 as a definite relative, so the ayah depends on the prior group in 18:100 instead of beginning with a new subject. Its frame then filters that group through two predicates: eyes in covering and an inability to hear. The ṣifa-or-badal pressure matters because the description can work as either qualification or re-identification, but the shared boundary antecedent remains fixed.

topics.headline: boundary-bound relative pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not start a fresh subject; its first word reaches back to the prior group in 18:100.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as a masculine plural relative pronoun whose antecedent is the group named in 18:100.

topics.headline: qualification or re-identification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relative can either narrow the prior class descriptively or restate it by the sensory diagnosis that follows.
topics.reason: The row preserves a real parse pressure, but the bundle only requires the antecedent relation, so the ṣifa versus badal force remains a qualified alternative.

topics.headline: two-predicate diagnostic filter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the referent is identified by two states together: covered eyes and failed hearing.
topics.reason: The attachment layer marks two kāna descriptions joined in the relative frame, matching the CRITICAL two-condition filter claim.

words.gloss_range: perfect copular state verb agreeing with the broken-plural eye subject
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}) makes the first diagnosis a settled copular state: the eyes are in a covering condition, not newly acted upon. Its feminine singular agreement attaches the state to the eye noun as a collective broken-plural subject, while the later plural state verb shifts the diagnosis from organs to people. At the boundary after 18:100, the displayed scene turns into anatomical and receptive diagnosis; the closed kāf onset and stopped final tāʾ give this state verb a clipped edge before the more open eye noun.
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and copular state; here selected as predicative existence in a condition

topics.headline: eye-level agreement before person-level shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first state belongs grammatically to the eyes, while the next state will move to the people themselves.
topics.reason: The feminine singular verb agrees with the broken-plural eye subject, and the later plural verb marks the subject shift.

topics.headline: settled locative eye-state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause describes the eyes as already located in a covering condition, not narrating a new act of covering.
topics.reason: The copular verb plus locative predicate supports a state reading; form-contrast rows correctly exclude reflexive or causative formation.

topics.headline: state language at the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a shift from the display in 18:100 into a diagnostic state measured by separation from remembrance and failed hearing.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and boundary rows cohere with the local state frame; 18:28 remains a contrast, not a controller of the parse.

topics.headline: clipped state onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact sound-shape of the state verb before the more open eye noun.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is modest but locally tied to the surface form and does not contradict grammar.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural eyes as the collective organ subject of the first state clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْيُنُهُمْ}} ({{tr:aʿyunuhum}}) is the possessed, nominative subject of the first state clause, so the covered site is their eyes rather than an abstract faculty alone. The broken plural and suffix make many organs one possessed perceptual field under a single cover, not each person's two eyes itemized. The wider root range is narrowed to eyes here, but spring, essence, and lookout senses help the reader feel why the eye is treated as a blocked aperture; this reverses same-surah eye motifs in 18:17 and 18:28. Its sound also moves from a deep opening toward nasal closure, matching the aperture-closing image.
words.root_gloss_range: eye, spring, essence, or lookout; here locally narrowed to eyes while preserving aperture imagery

topics.headline: possessed collective eye-field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that many possessed eyes are treated as one collective perceptual field under a single covering.
topics.reason: QAC marks a broken plural with possessive suffix as the subject of the first copular verb, and the singular cover supports the collective field reading.

topics.headline: eye as blocked aperture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local eye sense while also seeing why cover imagery can treat the eyes as blocked apertures of perception.
topics.reason: The local grammar selects physical eyes, so spring, essence, and lookout senses remain image-pressure rather than alternate translations.

topics.headline: same-surah eye motif reversed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surah moves from disciplined or visible eyes to eyes enclosed from remembrance, and then to failed hearing.
topics.reason: Rows with concrete references survive as motif contrast: 18:28 and 18:17 illuminate the eye language without overriding the local syntax.

topics.headline: aperture-closing sound contour
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sound contour of the word itself can be heard as opening and narrowing around the covered-eye image.
topics.reason: The sound rows are surface-specific and secondary, so they are retained as a candidate rather than an interpretive driver.

words.gloss_range: locative containment preposition, not a root-bearing lexical noun or verb
words.prose: the containment preposition gives the cover relation its geometry: the eyes are in the covering, not merely under a surface object. That first PP completes the locative predicate before the separative particle names separation from the remembrance relation. The short preposition therefore makes enclosure the base state and prepares the blocked-source phrase that follows.

topics.headline: containment rather than surface placement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the eyes are placed inside the covering, not merely under or behind it.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the cover noun as a locative predicate complement, supporting containment as the active relation.

topics.headline: location before separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause first establishes enclosure and only afterward names what the enclosure separates them from.
topics.reason: The attachment layer makes the first PP the predicate and the second PP the complement that supplies the blocked relation.

words.gloss_range: indefinite concrete cover or lid used as the predicated covering condition
words.prose: {{ar:غِطَآءٍ}} ({{tr:ghiṭāʾin}}) is the clause's diagnostic cover noun: indefinite, singular, and governed by the containment preposition, yet precise in function because the following separative remembrance phrase names what it blocks. Its concrete cover-or-lid image fits the eye as aperture; it suggests close overlay rather than distant partition, wrapping, or encasing, while agency is left unstated. The rare cover word also answers the display of 18:100 and contrasts with the cover removed in 50:22; the row that assigns that paired occurrence to 41:5 is rejected. Its long ā and final hamza give the cover word a recited catch at the ayah's center.
words.root_gloss_range: covering, overlay, lid, or concealment; here a concrete cover-image for perceptual blockage

topics.headline: indefinite cover as the diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cover is not a named object but a qualitative covering condition predicated of the eyes.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the locative preposition and indefinite by tanwīn, while the whole phrase functions as the predicate.

topics.headline: overlay-cover geometry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a close cover or lid image around the perceptive aperture, while agency remains unstated.
topics.reason: The concrete cover branch fits the local noun, but causative and reflexive family members only supply background pressure and do not become local events.

topics.headline: cover completed by remembrance target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cover is structurally incomplete until the clause names the remembrance relation it blocks.
topics.reason: The second prepositional phrase is licensed as complement after the cover noun or whole state, both preserving separation from the remembrance relation.

topics.headline: rare cover word at the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a marked cover word answers the display of 18:100 and contrasts with the cover removed in 50:22.
topics.reason: The rarity claim survives, but it is narrowed to the attested contrast with 50:22 and to the broader obstruction vocabulary around 41:5.

topics.headline: weighted cover sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the long, arrested sound of the cover word in the middle of the ayah.
topics.reason: The orthographic and phonetic rows are surface-specific and cohere with the cover-word center of the clause.

topics.blocking_evidence: QAC and contextual evidence mark the local cover as rare, while the paired cover contrast is with 50:22; 41:5 contains other obstruction vocabulary rather than the same cover noun.
topics.headline: wrong paired occurrence reference
topics.reason: The count-two rarity is usable, but the row identifies 41:5 as the paired occurrence; the stronger bundle evidence and other CRITICAL rows identify 50:22 for the cover-removal contrast.

words.gloss_range: separative preposition marking distance from the named remembrance relation
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) turns the cover from mere enclosure into separation from the remembrance word. It may specify the cover itself or the whole eye-state, but in either case the axis is avoidance-separation from the divine remembrance relation, not a bare source marker. The particle reopens the predicate after the cover noun so the reader learns what the covering prevents.

topics.headline: cover-specific or state-wide separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that separation from remembrance can specify either the cover itself or the whole covered-eye state.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses the complement after the cover phrase, while the CRITICAL rows preserve a real scope difference without forcing only one route.

topics.headline: directional separation from remembrance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns remembrance into the relation from which the cover holds them apart.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the remembrance noun and marks separation rather than mere source or topic in this cover construction.

words.gloss_range: definite first-person possessed verbal noun: remembrance, reminding, and reminder-relation
words.prose: {{ar:ذِكْرِي}} ({{tr:dhikrī}}) is a possessed maṣdar: definite through the first-person suffix and personal to the divine speaker inside a third-person diagnosis. The relation can be remembrance of God and reminder from God, so the cover blocks a two-way process of remembering, being reminded, and returning to awareness. The same phrase in 20:124 and same-surah scenes in 18:28 and 18:57 make this word a blocked endpoint of the remembrance thread. As the first beat closes, its dense dh-k-r cluster narrows into the slender possessive ī before the conjunction opens the hearing-failure clause.
words.root_gloss_range: remembering, mentioning, reminding, reminder, and scripture-related awareness; here possessed by the divine speaker

topics.headline: personal two-way remembrance relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the blocked relation is personal to the divine speaker and can run both as remembering God and as reminder from God.
topics.reason: The first-person suffix makes the verbal noun definite and relational; objective and subjective genitive pressures both survive, but neither should erase the other.

topics.headline: remembrance as active process
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is blocked is not a static label but a process of remembering, being reminded, and returning to awareness.
topics.reason: The maṣdar form licenses process and content together, while derived reminder and recall forms remain family pressure rather than local form replacement.

topics.headline: blocked endpoint of the remembrance thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a common remembrance field in the surah culminates here as the very relation from which perception is covered.
topics.reason: The rows with 20:124, 18:28, and 18:57 provide concrete contrast points: turning away, commanded attention, and reminder scenes become a covered-state diagnosis here.

topics.headline: first beat closes on possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first half closes on the possessed remembrance relation before the conjunction opens the hearing-failure half.
topics.reason: The word is the final content word before the conjunction, and its suffixal ending makes the personal relation audible at the beat boundary.

words.gloss_range: conjunction that can coordinate a second predicate or mark concurrent circumstance
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) binds the two diagnostic halves while preserving their difference. It can be read as coordination or as a circumstantial link, so the hearing failure is either a second cumulative predicate or the concurrent state accompanying the covered eyes. In both cases it is the hinge from visual cover to auditory incapacity.

topics.headline: coordination or concurrent circumstance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause is either a cumulative second diagnosis or the concurrent state accompanying the eye-covering.
topics.reason: The attachment layer marks coordination strongly, while the CRITICAL ḥāl reading remains a plausible interpretive pressure; the output keeps both without collapsing the clauses.

topics.headline: hinge from sight to hearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the conjunction as the hinge that binds visual covering and auditory incapacity into one perceptual profile.
topics.reason: The second kāna-clause is syntactically linked to the first while preserving a different subject and sensory domain.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural copular support returning the predicate to the human referents
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) returns the predicate to the human referents carried by the relative pronoun, not to the eyes. With the negator and the imperfect capacity verb, it makes inability a continuing group-state rather than one failed hearing event. The same state-language that framed the organs now frames the people themselves as unable to receive hearing; against 18:28, command-pressure has become incapacity-diagnosis.
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and copular state; here selected as persistent group-level predication

topics.headline: return from eyes to people
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second state is predicated of the people themselves, not of the eyes.
topics.reason: The masculine plural verb and pro-dropped subject continue the relative group and reverse the feminine eye agreement of the first clause.

topics.headline: habitual incapacity as group-state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the inability to hear is framed as a continuing characteristic state, not a single missed event.
topics.reason: The past copular support encloses negated imperfect capacity, and the attachment layer treats that predicate as the content under the second kāna clause.

topics.headline: being language recast as incapacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the surah’s state language landing here as a diagnosis of unavailable hearing rather than narrative circumstance.
topics.reason: The 18:28 contrast remains contextual: command pressure elsewhere is recast here as state-framed incapacity.

words.gloss_range: descriptive negation scoped over the capacity verb within the past-state frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) scopes over the capacity verb inside the past-state frame, so the clause denies ability to attain hearing rather than merely denying one sound or one occasion. It is descriptive negation, not prohibition or a lam-style jussive-past denial, and it leaves the following imperfect morphology exposed. The second clause is therefore organized around negated capacity.

topics.headline: negation of capacity, not one sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause denies the ability to attain hearing, not merely a particular act of hearing.
topics.reason: The negator falls directly on the capacity verb inside the past-state frame, preserving scope over the whole auditory predicate.

topics.headline: descriptive rather than prohibitive negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle reports an incapacity state rather than commanding them not to hear.
topics.reason: The imperfect remains descriptive under the copular frame; the row correctly excludes prohibitive or jussive-past force.

words.gloss_range: Form X capacity verb: ability to attain hearing, colored by compliance-root pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}} ({{tr:yastaṭīʿūna}}) names the failed capacity that stands between negation and the final hearing noun. Its Form X shape from {{ar:ط و ع}} ({{tr:ṭ-w-ʿ}}) keeps ordinary ability as the local sense while letting compliance-root pressure show: they cannot find inward yielding to reception. The same-surah contrast with 18:97 turns physical inability at the wall into perceptual inability here, and 18:28 supplies the obedience-command background that is now broken beside hearing. The emphatic ṭāʾ and extended ī-ū vowels make the capacity verb sound effortful while it names failed ability.
words.root_gloss_range: obedience, compliance, capacity, and ability; here Form X selects capacity while the root colors it as internal yielding

topics.headline: ongoing human capacity failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the human subjects are ongoing failed capacity-bearers, with hearing named as what their capacity cannot reach.
topics.reason: The verb is plural imperfect under the negated kāna frame and governs the hearing noun as object or specification.

topics.headline: Form X capacity as internal compliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ability is expressed through a compliance-root Form X, so failed hearing is also failed inward yielding to reception.
topics.reason: The local sense remains capacity, not direct obedience, but the root and Form X morphology legitimately color capacity as finding compliance within.

topics.headline: broken hearing-obedience formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb beside hearing decomposes the hearing-and-obedience pair into an inability formula.
topics.reason: The adjacency to the hearing noun makes the formulaic pressure local; 18:28 and 18:97 serve as concrete same-surah contrasts.

topics.headline: effortful capacity sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the length and weight of the capacity verb just as it names failed ability.
topics.reason: The sound observation is surface-specific and secondary but coheres with the long Form X verb.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative verbal noun naming hearing or receptive audition as the failed domain
words.prose: {{ar:سَمْعًا}} ({{tr:samʿan}}) closes the ayah on hearing as the unattained domain. As an indefinite accusative maṣdar after the capacity verb, it can be object or specification, but either way the failed target is receptive hearing itself, not a single heard item; the wording denies even basic reception before derived attentive listening is in view. The ayah has moved from covered eyes to unavailable hearing, redistributing the hearing-sight disability field known from 2:7, 16:108, and 45:23 and completing the broken hearing-obedience relation beside the capacity verb. The final tanwīn gives the closure a nasal fall as the ayah lands on failed auditory reception.
words.root_gloss_range: hearing, listening, audition, reception, and attentive intake; here the broad faculty/reception sense is negated

topics.headline: hearing itself as failed domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final noun denies hearing as an available faculty or domain, not only a specific sound.
topics.reason: The indefinite accusative maṣdar after the capacity verb can function as object or specification; both readings make hearing the failed target.

topics.headline: reception broader than sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local sense is basic receptive hearing, broad enough to include listening-response but not narrowed to a derived attentive-listening form.
topics.reason: The maṣdar selects broad reception; causative and intentional-listening derivatives remain family background and are not the local form.

topics.headline: visual opening and auditory closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens with eyes and closes on hearing, framing the whole description as cross-sensory receptive failure.
topics.reason: The structure distributes sight and hearing across two clauses; broader hearing-sight formulas at 2:7, 16:108, and 45:23 are relevant contrast points.

topics.headline: hearing-obedience reversal completed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final hearing noun completes the broken hearing-and-obedience relation begun by the capacity verb.
topics.reason: The local adjacency of the capacity verb and hearing noun makes the formulaic reversal concrete, not merely distributional.

topics.headline: nasal final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final nasal fall as the ayah lands on failed auditory reception.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows are surface-specific and tied to the final word position.
